builds.howItPlays: You pick your strongest unit each turn and exhaust Shen to make it Tank, so it has to take the hit before anything else of yours can be touched. You hold your battlefields turn after turn, using hidden tricks and stuns to keep that one protected unit alive while your opponent runs out of ways to get through.
builds.whyYou: You like protecting one thing and refusing to let it go. You're patient enough to hold your ground for a long time, and you enjoy the moment your opponent finally can't find an answer to your defense. If a slow, grinding win where you barely take real damage feels satisfying, Shen is your Legend.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 1: riftboundguide.com says Shen wants to 'hold key battlefields by keeping his most important unit alive turn after turn' rather than 'closing the game out fast,' summing up 'if you would rather grind out a long game than race to end it, Shen is the pick.' stance 1: skillshotzgaming.com rates Shen's approach explicitly 'Reactive,' calling it a 'straightforward stall plan'; riftboundguide.com agrees it's primarily 'defensive control.' complexity 6: skillshotzgaming.com rates complexity 'High' while riftboundguide.com calls it 'moderate,' driven by choosing which unit to protect each turn and playing around Hidden tricks; split the difference. variance 2.5: skillshotzgaming.com rates variance 'Low,' and riftboundguide.com agrees Tank gives 'consistent, reliable protection rather than creating dramatic swings.' Legend ability: exhaust Shen to give a friendly unit Tank for the turn, forcing the opponent to assign combat damage to it first. Confidence: high, two sources agree closely on every axis. Reviewer should double-check starterDeck: corrected from the seed's generic 'Vendetta Showdown Deck' to the exact product 'Vendetta Showdown Deck: Zed vs Shen,' which bundles two full 56-card decks rather than a single-Legend starter; confirm that framing is acceptable for this field.
